bill.title: A bill to require the Secretary of Transportation to revise certain Federal motor vehicle safety standards to advance tire technologies, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of Transportation to update federal safety standards for motor vehicle tires to reflect advances in tire technology. The bill does not specify which technologies or standards would be revised, making it difficult to determine the precise scope of the changes.

industries.rationale: Tire manufacturers would face revised federal safety standards affecting product design and compliance obligations.
Trucking and logistics companies would be affected by new tire safety requirements for their vehicle fleets.
Automotive retailers and tire dealers may face changes in the products they can sell and stock.

plain.everydayEffect: Nothing has changed yet. The title alone does not say what would change for you, and this tool will not guess. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
